The game is A LOT of fun, the puzzles are even more varied than it takes two, and even more impressive: The game is visually EVEN more impressive.  Its creative, varied, long, emotional. the only thing it is not, is subtle in its storytelling. I really like the protagonists.

Mina the Hollower is an insanely fun, top-down action adventure that rewards curiosity, exploration and those who master its burrowing mechanic. Its 8-bit art style and colorful environments are eye catching and easy to pick apart and its soundtrack is excellent!
Don't let its simple appearance fool you though; this game can be tough, especially in the early game. The combat is fast and positioning is everything. It can be tedious and punishing; and the platforming can require pixel perfect timing.

As a whole, its a fantastic game with great replayability.

Very cool. Story was delightful. Narrator was great. Combat is straightforward. Decent game.
The midgame sidequesting before the moles was a little boring and I hated going up and down and up and down the sewers. Other than that, not bad pace wise.
Art is beautiful along with a great soundtrack that matches the vibes of the setting. Long Tail Village almost reminds me of Rivendell. The bard's tune during the first crypt boss fight is a banger too (reminds me of Hades). 
Overall, not a must play but if you must play it, it is enjoyable.
the only good things in the game are the visuals and music, the rest is just ♥♥♥♥.
can't wait for future content updates & full campaign, god speed for devs <3

Artstyle hmmmm immaculate
Story was very basic, even for a fairy tale, i didnt want justifications, since i viewed it as a fairy tale but yehh even as a bedtime story it was lacking.
I could see where the devs run out of budget, since the starting regions had bossfights and the undead region as well had set up for a bossfight beetween the song and the monster who wanted silence, but she was skipped, i thought every region would follow the example of the nobodyvile and i think that was the intention of the devs too. But later regions started getting exponencially smaller and having less stakes, which i guess isnt ideal for climaxing the story.
Anyway...
Music and Art Direction are positivily INSPIRED, more plz, hope the studio thrives <3

A fun short side-scrolling action RPG. The world is charming, the story is told in a heart-warming fashion and the entire thing is fairly uncomplicated. There's way more skills than the game's length supports in terms of leveling, but that just means there's always room for growth. There is too much swimming, though.

This game is not perfect. It's had it's fair share of ups and downs, and moments when things have seemed impossibly bleak. However, in the end, there is simply no other game like this one - and while the future of the game is unknown, the community has made their own fate by refusing to let it die. When the game becomes whole after the promises of September 21st, 2026, this game will genuinely be one of the greatest experiences you could find, anywhere.

I like the silliness but it isn't too silly to a point where it's brain-rot. It's fit for all ages, 1-100!

I try not to give negative reviews, but I cannot in good faith give this game a recommendation. The graphics are gorgeous, I love the gameplay, but this is a gacha game. I love  gacha games. The pull rates are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ATROCIOUS. I threw actual money at this to test it, and $30 got me NOTHING. ZILCH. I got a bunch of food and that's IT. I looked into it, and it turns out the pull rates are rigged so you HAVE to spend minimum of $500 to get clothes-- but only in the US! In China, THIS IS NOT AN ISSUE. This is genuinely predatory to people with gambling addictions, which is likely their intent to begin with.

I adore this game! (clearly since it's been my pfp for years) It's a pretty short game, tends to take 4 or so hours less if your not going for platinum.

I will say that the third chapter has a tendency to glitch which can be pretty frustrating so a tip for anyone playing is to save frequently. Besides that it's a solid game, the developers tend to put it and the others on sale quite a bit in spring so I'd recommend waiting till then if you want to play it

There’s a reason I refer to my Steam Deck as a $500 Balatro machine. Sure I play other games in my library but no game is as addictive and easily accessible as Balatro. It’s the perfect game to play casually on the couch while watching tv. That is until the numbers start to go brrrr and you lock in for the run. Laughably I put in over 58 hours before I found the right combination of Jokers and suit levels to finally win my first run. The 57 hours it took me til that I was unbothered that I’d yet to complete a run try as I might. Why go so long without winning? Because the game is so simple a concept to learn yet so addictive to master it just gets its hooks into you. 

Just get the game.

Simple game with a short story that was able to be a good game. It's a game where you make your own decisions, so each character is going through their own situations, and you must choose what you will answer on these situations. There's kind of a story on this game about the main character, which is the killer, that decided to kill his sister, because of his problematic childhood and stuff.

I liked this game, it's kind of repetitive, but it's not bad: The characters are well written; there's a good story behind them in each dialogue; the gameplay is simple and it's really fun exploring the house, even though it takes around 10 minutes to beat the game.

Looked interesting, enjoyed the first couple minutes where you play as Noa and choose your cat. The shift to present day and then to 1999 were questionable. Then add the NPC in the library constantly telling me where to find the objects I'm looking for while I am actively picking up the items was annoying. If these were the only issues I would still try the full game when it came out, but the use of generative AI and comments made by the studio co-founder have taken this game off my radar and my interest is now zero. Unfortunate.

100% garbage from Crapsoft. Buggy. Desync issues. Game assets don't load all the time for co-op play both in game and in cutscenes. Grainy graphics even when you have all these craptastic video setting turned off. Lags almost all the time. I was waiting for it to get good, but that never happened. Crapsoft really dropped the ball on this game. Not worth even getting this on sale. You are way better off just playing the Master Chief collection. The bonus missions werre meh, and didn't really add any depth to the story. Save your money, save your time, and save yourself from experiencing Crapsoft's crappy game. The only fun I had was to party up with my friends. The game itself was nothing special. Wait. It was special. It was special in being a crappy game from Crapsoft.

Sick old school shot em up, artstyle is amazing, sound design is literally flawless,bosses are a total highlight with a lot of character reminded me a bit on dead rising psychos at times,awesome setting and guns. I do think the control sheme aint perfect and it would have been nice to be able to map cover and melee on buttons.

Overall probably among my favorite "newer" retro games along with SoR4

Besides the fact this game has no one playing it. My friend and I bought the game. We had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. The bots do try to murder you if they are the killer. They do collect resources and hoard them sometimes. This game is fun to play with friends. A dead game is only dead until people revive it. Does it need some optimization? Yeah, a bit, there is a delay in when the game announces someone dies. A mic bug that's solved by leaving the lobby and coming back. Those are my biggest issues. However, I love the look of it cause it's like those old PS2 games honestly. I've seen worse graphics. This game is fun and we bought it on a sale. Major props to the Dev who kept putting out content and bug fixes when the game slowed down. Even put out a Halloween event. I hope it comes out this year too, cause I would like to play it with my friends.

It's not bad, but it's so repetitive... all screens in an area look almost the same. The animation is smooth and the background graphics are charming, but the "sprites" look too flat. The sound is what it is—not good, not bad. Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game because it feels like you are walking through the same screen 100 times, but as I said, it's not a bad game per se.

Cinematic masterpiece. It's not a true XCOM successor, but a great game in its own right, and I was locked in from start to end. All of the supporting cast are great and I cared both for them and the general plot. It sometimes felt like watching a really good TV show.

Warmly recommend and wish the furloughed devs some relief due to this title's well-earned success. I hope we see more content for this game, or an eventual sequel!
